Streetlights are present along both sides of the road, which may improve nighttime visibility and perceived security.
No sidewalk, guardrail, or separated pedestrian space is visible beside the travel lanes, increasing exposure risk for people walking near the roadway edge.
The long straight alignment and open road character can encourage higher vehicle speeds, which raises crash severity risk for all non-motorized users.

The surrounding greenery improves environmental quality, but the absence of human-scale facilities limits practical day-to-day livability.
sustainability: Tree planting and vegetated road edges contribute some ecological value and visual greening.
The absence of visible bike lanes, sidewalks, or public transport facilities suggests the corridor mainly supports car-dependent travel rather than low-carbon mode choice.
